messages.text: I’ll read the story and all files listed in its context, then implement and verify the audit and restart behavior.

The existing commands already write the seven required audit actions atomically. I’m adding the administrator query and safe display, then a backup CLI and verification that compares the database across two distinct Waitress processes.

The audit query now enforces administrator access within its read transaction, and the page handles filters, empty results, errors, and expired access. Tests are checking that repeat operations add no audit rows and that the backup captures committed WAL data without overwriting an existing file.

The new tests pass: all seven actions have complete snapshots, retries leave audit counts unchanged, corrupt JSON returns a safe 500, and the backup includes committed WAL data while excluding an uncommitted write. The restart and full-route permission checks are now running against a real Waitress server.

The restart check passed: a new Waitress PID read identical business records, slots, audit rows, and relationship hashes. Old sessions remained valid, and replaying the original intent returned the same cancelled booking without adding audit rows. All 138 route-permission cases passed, as did 201 Python and 296 JavaScript tests. The audit page also passed Chromium checks at both screen sizes.

The performance rerun passed with zero errors and P95 of 21.5 ms across 200 measured requests. The existing concurrency and rollback checks also passed. Several older browser runners could not launch their default Chromium, so I preserved those incomplete runs and restarted them with the installed Chrome executable.

All six existing browser workflows passed with Chrome, including room management, booking and intent replay, both cancellation paths, and maintenance creation and revocation. I’ve saved the acceptance summary and backup/restore instructions, and marked the story ready for the main workflow’s independent review.

Story 3.4 is implemented and marked `review`.

- Added the admin audit API, strict DTOs, filtering UI, safe expandable snapshots, and shared authentication-loss handling.
- Added SQLite backup CLI with exclusive targets, 0600 permissions, integrity checks, and documented recovery steps.
- Passed **201 Python tests**, **296 JavaScript tests**, **138 route-permission cases**, both audit browser sizes, and six existing browser workflows.
- Passed real Waitress restart, old-session/intent replay, concurrency and rollback checks. Performance P95: **21.501 ms**, zero errors.

Evidence: [verification.md](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/docs/evidence/story-3.4/verification.md), [acceptance-summary.json](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/outputs/group-room-booking/docs/evidence/story-3.4/acceptance-summary.json).

No known product work remains. Independent review and parent-owned recording/materials remain; disaster recovery was documented, not claimed as exercised. Earlier failed verification attempts remain preserved. No Git operations were performed.
